An army officer who seized power in Dahomey on 26 October 1972, ending a decade of six coups, and ruled until 1991, then again as an elected president from 1996 to 2006.

In 1974 he declared the country Marxist-Leninist, and in 1975 renamed it the People's Republic of Benin. State control and debt brought the economy to collapse by the late 1980s, and unpaid students and civil servants went on strike. In 1990 he called a national conference, which took away his powers and led to the election of Nicephore Soglo in 1991. He accepted defeat, came back by vote in 1996 and stepped down at the end of his term. See also the Cold War and Vodun.
sum: An army officer who seized power in Dahomey on 26 October 1972, ending a decade of six coups, and ruled until 1991, then again as an elected president from 1996 to 2006.
